header.title: Architecting Enterprise AgentOps: Scalable Topologies, Governance Gates, and A2A Interoperability
header.subtitle: AI in 5 Days (DAY5) • Architect Track • For Rafee Mohamed

textParagraph.text: Transitioning autonomous agentic systems from prototype to production requires closing the 80% 'last mile' gap through an enterprise-grade operational discipline known as AgentOps. For systems architects, this shifts the paradigm from traditional MLOps to orchestrating stateful, non-deterministic execution paths, requiring strict evaluation-gated CI/CD pipelines, decoupled stateless runtimes on Cloud Run or Vertex AI Agent Engine, and externalized state persistence across AlloyDB and long-term memory stores. Production resilience hinges on a three-tier defense-in-depth framework—anchoring System Instructions as a behavioral constitution, utilizing Agent Gateway and Model Armor for real-time policy and injection filtering, and deploying runtime circuit breakers. At organizational scale, system modularity is achieved through a dual-protocol topology: leveraging the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for structured, deterministic tool execution and the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol with Agent Cards for distributed, cross-team autonomous goal delegation.

decoratedText.text: Why do traditional microservice rate-limiters and autoscalers fail to prevent cost runaways and cascade failures when agents dynamically assemble their own runtime execution trajectories?

Spend 15 minutes drafting an architecture boundary specification for a multi-agent workflow: define the exact interface boundary where A2A high-level task delegation hands off to MCP deterministic tool execution, and design an automated circuit-breaker pattern (using feature flags and Secret Manager) that can instantaneously quarantine a compromised external tool without taking down the root agent runtime.
